summary: The web publisher supports individually approved, revocable browser grants for message sending while retaining its read-only server bearer. Request secrets and 30-day device credentials remain in protected HttpOnly cookies. Raw daemon pairing routes are blocked at the browser gateway; only publisher endpoints can redeem credentials. Revoked or expired grants return the browser to pairing without discarding saved drafts.

replay.detail: No daemon replay or projection rebuild is introduced by this web change.

schema.detail: No database schema change. Browser credentials use Secure, SameSite=Strict, HttpOnly cookies scoped to Path=/; request cookies expire after five minutes and device cookies after 30 days.

rules.detail: No checkpoint or fleet coordination rule change.

compatibility.detail: Browser sending requires the matching daemon browser-request, redemption and current-device revocation endpoints. Non-publisher and replay hosts retain existing compose behavior. Direct browser access to daemon pairing and pairings endpoints is refused, including encoded and ambiguous paths.

downtime.detail: No interruption beyond the normal publisher upgrade restart is required.

manual.detail: Keep the publisher bearer read-only and restrict pairing admission to personal tailnet logins. Custom server overlays must configure the documented pairing admission callback. Each browser requests approval and compares its displayed code with Fractal; browser labels and login names are not proof of the requester.

recovery.detail: Forget this browser revokes its device grant and clears pairing cookies. Revoked or expired credentials are cleared when status is checked. Rolling back the publisher restores its previous fixed-bearer behavior and does not migrate daemon state; existing browser grants remain subject to daemon expiry and revocation.
